newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-Portugal's Champalimaud advances bank revamp.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Portugal's Champalimaud advances bank revamp.

text.p: The Champalimaud group buyout for its Credito Predial Portugues is part of the overall restructuring of its financial holdings, with majority control the clear aim, analysts said on Wednesday.

They said the pricing, 1,800 escudos per share, was too low to tempt small investors so the bid must have been agreed ahead of time with at least one major stakeholder who wanted to get out, or at least reduce his holding.

There has been in the past market talk that the Champalimaud group, which already controls some 49 percent of CPP, might be interested eventually in selling the bank to another Portuguese institution -- and Banco Espirito Santo has been named.
But the analysts dismissed the possibility that the offered buyout was an attempt to put together a majority holding with the future aim of selling it.

"To sell the housing credit arm of a financial group -- an area that has always been profitable -- does not seem very likely for someone who is looking to consolidate their financial sector strategy," said Luis Valadas of Espirito Santo Research.

"CPP is a pretty valuable institution because it operates in an expanding market with good clients and margins. For these reasons, it is particulary important for the (Champalimaud) group," said another analyst who asked not to be named.

The Champalimaud group announced on Tuesday night that its two main banks Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor and Banco Totta & Acores, together with group financial holding Mundial Confianca were launching the CPP buyout.
Other major shareholders in CPP include Macau businessman Stanley Ho, who has some 20 percent, and construction group Mague with some five percent. The free float is only around 15 percent.
Analysts said that Mague could be the most likely candidate to sell because it no longer had any other interests in the financial sector.

The Champalimaud group said the buyout price took account of the three billion escudo capital increase, raising capital to 33 billion, being launched at the same time at the same price of 1,800 escudos per share.
The stock, which had closed at 2,075 escudos on Tuesday, was trading at 1,930 escudos on Wednesday, up from an early low of 1,850. No date has yet been set for either the buyout or the capital call.
Analysts said the buyout price did not fully reflect the worth of the bank.
"The price is not really attractive. The value of the share adjusted for the capital call would be 2,050 escudos," said Valadas, based on Tuesday's closing level.
Some analysts said the market price even understated the real value of the bank given the fact that it operated in a high-growth part of the market.
"The price is excellent for the buyer because CPP is worth much more. We put its value at around 3,200 escudos," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

For Pedro Assuncao of Central Banco de Investimentos the buyout formed part of the overall restructuring of the group's financial interests which has already seen closer ties between Banco Sotto and Banco Totta.
"But I also believe that there could be deep changes in Credito Predial Portugues, more than those that are being announced, beyond the total refocusing on mortgage lending," he said.
Inigo Lucabarri of Salomon Brothers in London said that increasing stakes in subsidiary banks made a great deal of financial sense at a time of falling interest rates.
"It is a very rational move," she said. "Nothing more."
($1=185 escudos)
--Lisbon bureau 3511-3150035
